# avd_ops_reader.ps1

<!-- Generated by scripts/Update-BrainDocs.ps1 from the code. Do not edit; edit the code and regenerate. -->

avd-ops-reader -- the optional read-only identity for unattended avd-current-state runs: set it up, check it, remove it (docs/reader-identity.md).

Optional. The collector, validator and facts script never need it: with no reader they use your own sign-in, as always. The reader is for runs with nobody signed in, such as a weekly collection from GitHub Actions in your private repo, and it reads with Reader instead of your own rights. - App-only, single tenant, no secret and no certificate. GitHub Actions signs in as it through a federated credential bound to one private repo and one environment, by GitHub's immutable subject (numeric owner and repo IDs), so a deleted or renamed repo's name can't be reused to get a token. - An app management policy blocks passwords and keys on the app, so not even an owner or an app administrator can add a secret later. - Roles: Reader on the subscriptions or resource groups you name; opt-in Log Analytics Reader on one workspace, Cost Management Reader, and Storage Blob Data Contributor on one container for the run's output. No directory (Graph) permission; that is a separate decision. - One reader for the family: each private repo that runs reads gets its own federated credential on the same app (Entra allows 20). Writes never use it. Personal project, not for production use. Provided as is, without warranty of any kind (MIT License, see LICENSE). Not affiliated with the author's employer, with Liquidware or with Microsoft. MODES ------------------------------------------------------------------ Initialize Creates or updates the reader. Run by a person: an Application Developer (or anyone, when users may register apps) for the app, plus Owner, User Access Administrator or a condition-limited Role Based Access Control Administrator on each scope. The policy step needs an Application Administrator; when you aren't one it prints the command for one. Never needs Global Administrator. Test Checks the reader (the default). Signed in as a person: everything. Signed in as the reader itself (in the workflow): only its role assignments, which is all it can read. Remove Deletes the reader's role assignments, the policy, the service principal and the app, and prints what it removed. Runs in Azure Cloud Shell (PowerShell, or Bash through pwsh) and in PowerShell 7 on Windows, macOS and Linux, with Az.Accounts. Uses ARM and Graph REST through Invoke-AzRestMethod, so the one Az sign-in covers both.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `-Mode` | string | no | `'Test'` |  |
| `-Repo` | string[] | no | `@()` | Private repos (owner/name) whose workflows may sign in as the reader. |
| `-Environment` | string | no | `'avd-reader'` | The GitHub Environment the workflow runs in. Restrict it to the main branch in the repo's settings. |
| `-RepoId` | string | no |  | GitHub's numeric IDs, when GitHub can't show a private repo without a sign-in (one -Repo only). |
| `-OwnerId` | string | no |  |  |
| `-Subscription` | string[] | no | `@()` | Subscriptions (name or ID) for Reader. With -ResourceGroup, the one subscription those groups are in. |
| `-ResourceGroup` | string[] | no | `@()` | Resource groups for Reader instead of the whole subscription (needs exactly one -Subscription). |
| `-LogAnalyticsWorkspace` | string[] | no | `@()` | Log Analytics workspace resource IDs for Log Analytics Reader (opt-in; they hold sign-in data). |
| `-Cost` | switch | no |  | Cost Management Reader on the same subscriptions (opt-in). |
| `-OutputContainer` | string | no |  | A blob container's resource ID for the run's output (opt-in: Storage Blob Data Contributor there only). |
| `-AppName` | string | no | `'avd-ops-reader'` |  |
| `-ClientId` | string | no | `$env:AVD_READER_CLIENT_ID` | The reader's client ID. The app is found by this only, never by its name. |

## Examples

```powershell
./avd_ops_reader.ps1 -Mode Initialize -Repo contoso/avd-runs -Subscription 'AVD Production'
```
```powershell
pwsh -NoLogo -Command './avd_ops_reader.ps1 -Mode Test'
```
